status: EXPLORATORY capability/regime-boundary demo (not vs deployed v5)

env.dynamics: momentum + wall-bounce + two objects; nonlinear in pixel space

note: Per-pixel GBR omitted: one tree ensemble per output pixel does not scale, which is itself why raw-pixel regimes need a neural world model. Linear ridge is the scalable non-neural baseline.

cnn_plain_mse.note: plain MSE collapses toward copy on sparse-change pixels; matches the linear blur

verdict: CNN GPU wins the pixel regime: dynamic-region MAE 0.2358 vs ridge 0.5810 (+59% vs ridge) vs persistence 0.8329
honest_tradeoff: The change-weighted CNN wins decisively on the DYNAMIC region (moving objects): dyn MAE 0.236 vs ridge 0.581 (-59%) vs persistence 0.833. It trades a little static-background fidelity for this (overall-frame MAE 0.039 vs persistence 0.021 / ridge 0.031) because the loss up-weights changed pixels; the plain-MSE CNN avoids the trade (overall 0.021) but then only ties ridge on dynamics (0.536). Closed-loop rollout is stable for the CNN (~0.04 over 10 steps) while persistence degrades (0.017->0.056), so the CNN advantage grows with horizon. Net: in the raw-pixel regime a GPU neural world model is the only one that substantially predicts the nonlinear object dynamics; linear/tree models cannot (and per-pixel GBR does not scale).
